resources.string: No alert is not a guarantee of safety.
Kavach matches conversations against known scam patterns. It cannot tell you for certain what is happening.
Kavach is off. Start it when you are on a call you are unsure about.
Kavach is watching for %1$d kinds of scam tactic. None of them has come up.
%1$d of the %2$d tactic families used in scam scripts have come up. That is not proof of anything — it is a reason to slow down.
This matches a known scam script
Kavach is not certain, and cannot end the call. Do these three things.
Hang up. You can always call back on a number you trust.
Never share an OTP, PIN or password. No real bank or officer will ask.
Report it: call the cybercrime helpline 1930.
No demo scripts are packaged in this build.
Shown while Kavach is listening. Required by Android, and by us.
Kavach works without this. Adding the model lets it reason about a conversation as well as match patterns.
Download the model in your browser. It is large, so use wi-fi.
Then bring the downloaded file into Kavach.
Remove model and free the space
Not installed. Kavach is still fully working.
Kavach has no internet permission, so it cannot download this itself — your browser does, and you hand the file over. Nothing you say ever leaves the phone.
Optional. Without it Kavach uses its built-in pattern engine, which is what catches the scams in our tests.

Then put the call on speaker
A warning needs %1$d different families, not one loud one. That is what keeps a real bank fraud desk from setting it off.

Metadata only — timestamp, tactics, score, duration. No audio and no transcript were recorded, so none can be shared.

Kavach matches conversations against known scam patterns. It does not determine that a crime occurred, and no alert is not a guarantee of safety. Report suspected fraud in India on the cybercrime helpline 1930.
%1$d more families would raise this to a warning

Kavach reads nothing. This service exists only because Android mutes an ordinary app\'s microphone during a call, and an accessibility service is the one documented exception. No screen content, text or key press is ever read.
Lets Kavach hear a call. Reads nothing.
Shown when a call matches a known scam pattern. Bypasses Do Not Disturb.
What Kavach can do right now
Android blocks this toggle for apps installed outside an app store. Open App info, tap the three dots at the top right, and choose “Allow restricted settings”, then come back.
